build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: A persistent beat indicator (pulsing icon, metronome bar, or bouncing marker) shows the current rhythm. The player moves on the grid by pressing a direction key in time with the beat. Perfect-timing inputs flash gold and move the character smoothly; off-beat inputs show a different colour and cause a stumble animation with a wasted turn. Score 0 if there is no beat indicator, if movement is not grid-based, or if timing has no effect on movement success.

Attacking an adjacent enemy on-beat deals full damage with a visible hit effect (slash, flash, particles). Off-beat attacks deal reduced damage with a weaker visual. Enemies have distinct rhythm patterns: they telegraph attacks on specific beats with a wind-up animation, and the player must move or block on the correct beat to avoid damage. Score 0 if attacks have no timing component, if enemies have no rhythmic patterns, or if there is no visual distinction between on-beat and off-beat hits.

Defeated enemies drop gold or equipment. Equipment (weapons, armour) can be collected and visibly changes the player's attack pattern or sprite. A shop or chest between floors offers purchasable upgrades. At least 3 different equipment items exist with distinct gameplay effects. Score 0 if enemies drop nothing, if there is no equipment system, or if equipment has no visible effect.

At least 4 visually distinct enemy types with different rhythm behaviours: varying attack frequencies, movement patterns, and telegraph timings. Each enemy type has a unique sprite and animation set. The player must adapt their rhythm strategy to each enemy type. Score 0 if there are fewer than 4 enemy types, if enemies all behave identically, or if enemy types are not visually distinguishable.

The dungeon has at least 3 distinct floor themes (e.g., crypt, cavern, fortress) with different tile sets, background art, and enemy compositions. Floors are procedurally arranged or hand-crafted with visible variety. Score 0 if there is only one visual theme, if floors look identical, or if there are fewer than 3 distinct environments.

At least one boss encounter exists with a multi-beat attack pattern that differs from regular enemies. The boss has a unique large sprite, a health bar, and telegraphs a sequence of attacks the player must dodge rhythmically. The boss fight feels climactic and distinct from normal combat. Score 0 if there is no boss, if the boss behaves like a regular enemy, or if the boss has no multi-beat pattern.

Difficulty escalates across floors: later floors have faster tempos, more complex enemy patterns, or tighter timing windows. The player perceives a clear progression in challenge. At least 5 distinct floor levels are playable. Score 0 if difficulty is flat throughout, if there are fewer than 5 floors, or if later floors feel identical to early ones.

The HUD displays: current beat indicator with timing feedback, player health, current floor number, and gold count. All elements are readable and non-overlapping at 1280x720. The beat indicator is prominent and always visible during gameplay. Score 0 if any core HUD element is missing or if the beat indicator is not clearly visible.

Timing feedback is immediate and clear: perfect hits produce a distinct visual reward (gold flash, particle burst), good hits show a lesser effect, and misses show a negative indicator (red flash, stumble). The player can assess their timing quality from any single frame during an action. Score 0 if there is no timing feedback, or if perfect and missed hits look identical.

The full game loop is connected: Title screen -> Enter dungeon -> Move and fight on beat -> Collect loot -> Descend floors -> Fight boss -> Victory or death. The player can experience every node without restarting the application. Score 0 if any transition in the chain is missing or broken.

A title screen is present and styled: it shows the game name in a custom or themed font, has at minimum a play button that is interactive and transitions to the game, and uses a non-default background (dungeon scene, torchlit corridor, or illustrated artwork) — not plain plain grey or a solid-colour fill. Score 0 if the game launches directly into gameplay with no title screen, or if the start button is non-functional. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Overall art-style coherence: every visible element — dungeon tiles, player character, enemies, items, UI panels — belongs to a single consistent visual language (e.g., all pixel-art, all hand-drawn, all flat-vector). The palette is dark and atmospheric; no clashing neon or unrelated photorealistic assets. Score 0 if the screen mixes incompatible styles, or if elements are obviously unthemed placeholder shapes.

Environment, character, and UI art quality: dungeon floors use textured or illustrated tiles with visible detail; the player character is a recognisable animated sprite; enemies have distinct sprites per type; the beat indicator and HUD use styled, themed widgets. Score 0 if the dungeon is a uniform colour fill, if the player is a solid-colour primitive, or if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled default widgets.

Animation continuity and polish: beat pulses, movement transitions, attack slashes, enemy telegraphs, hit effects, loot pickups, and floor transitions each play as smooth multi-frame tweens or sprite animations — no element snaps to its new state in a single frame. Scene transitions use a brief fade or wipe rather than an instant cut. Score 0 if any of these moments is instantaneous, or if transitions are hard cuts with no tween.
